$comment: One component, the repository root: the version lives in Cargo.toml, and release-please's `rust` strategy updates Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock together — which is the pair that has to agree for `--locked` to work anywhere. dashboard/package.json is deliberately not a second component: the bundle is embedded in the binary and ships with it, so a separate dashboard version would be a second number nobody deploys. `include-component-in-tag` keeps the tag bare `vX.Y.Z` rather than `partner-portal-vX.Y.Z`: the tag is the artifact's name, and `deploy/rolling-update.sh` and the release jobs take it as the version they publish. The title pattern is pinned scopeless on purpose, not as a style choice: release-please's default is `chore${scope}: release${component} ${version}` and it fills `${scope}` with the TARGET BRANCH, so a Release PR would arrive titled `chore(main): release 0.1.0` — and `main` is not one of the scopes commitlint.config.mjs declares, because it is not an area of the code at all. The pattern matters twice over: it is the PR title AND the commit message release-please writes (the commit message is the title string), and the commit-msg hook checks both. Scopeless `chore: release 0.1.0` passes; every restatement of the default fails.
